### Quick‑Start Guide: Adding Profile Photo Uploads with Supabase **without writing code**

> **What you’ll need**
> * A Supabase account (free tier is fine)
> * Your project’s **URL** and **anonymous key** (you can find these in the Supabase dashboard → Settings → API)
> * A website builder that plugs into Supabase (e.g., [Stacker](https://stacks.io/), [Directus](https://directus.io/), or [Appwrite + Webflow](https://www.webflow.com/blog/webflow-appwrite)).
> * A basic HTML page (if you prefer to hand‑edit slightly).

Below is a no‑code, step‑by‑step workflow using **Stacker** (the easiest for beginners). If you prefer *Directus* or *Webflow*, let me know and I’ll translate the steps.

---

## 1️⃣ Set Up Supabase Storage for Profile Pictures

1. **Log in** to [Supabase](https://supabase.com/).  
2. Click on your project → **Storage**.  
3. Click **Create bucket**.  
   * Name: `profile_photos`  
   * **Public**: checked (so anyone can view the photo)  
   * **Conflict handling**: “Overwrite” (this makes “photo.png” → “photo_1.png” if you upload the same name again).

4. Inside the bucket, click **Add file** → **Upload folder** → create a folder named `users` (optional but keeps things tidy).

> **Tip**: You can delete the `public` permission later if you want to hide the images behind a signed URL, but for a simple profile‑photo use‑case public access is fine.

---

## 2️⃣ Add Authentication (Optional but recommended)

1. Still inside your Supabase project → **Authentication** → **Settings** → **General**.  
2. Enable **email sign‑up** and **magic link** (so users can create an account).  
3. Under **Security** → **Settings**, click “Add rule strategy” and choose **Email / Password**.  

With authentication you’ll know which user is uploading and can attach an ID to the photo.

---

## 3️⃣ Connect Stacker (or another no‑code builder)

### 3.1 Sign up or log in to Stacker
* Visit https://stacks.io/ and sign up with your Supabase credentials (or email).

### 3.2 Create a new app
1. On the Stacker dashboard, click **New app**.  
2. Choose **Supabase** as your data source.  
3. Paste your **Project URL** and **anon key**.  
4. Stacker will auto‑import all tables and storage buckets.

### 3.3 Add a “Profile” Page
1. In the App Builder → **Pages**, click **+ Add Page** → **Form**.  
2. Name it `My Profile`.  
3. Choose the **users** table (Supabase Auth creates one automatically).  
4. **Make the form read‑only** so people only edit their own data.  
5. Drag‑and‑drop fields:  
   * `avatar_url` (or create a new column)  
   * Any other user info you want to display.

### 3.4 Make the Avatar Field an Image Uploader
1. Click the `avatar_url` field in the form.  
2. Change **Field Type** → **Image**.  
3. Under **Storage**, pick the `profile_photos` bucket you created.  
4. Enable **Auto‑save** so the upload is linked to the user’s record automatically.

### 3.5 Set Visibility Rules
1. In the page settings → **Permissions**, set the rule:  
   * `is_authenticated == true` (only signed‑in users can see/edit)  
2. Optionally add a check to ensure a user can only edit their own row:  
   * `user.id === auth.uid` (Stacker handles this automatically for Auth‑based tables).

---

## 4️⃣ (Optional) Add Custom Folder Structure & Naming

If you want each photo to go into `profile_photos/users/<user‑id>/`, you can:

1. In Stacker → **Settings** → **Storage**, set the **Storage Path** to  
   `profile_photos/users/{{user.id}}/{{filename}}`.  
2. This keeps each user’s photos in a private sub‑folder, even if the bucket itself is public.

---

## 5️⃣ Test It Out!

1. Open your Stacker app (a link is given after publish).  
2. Sign up/sign in.  
3. Click **My Profile** → **Upload** the file → hit **Save**.  
4. The image should now appear next to your info.  
5. Hover over the image → you’ll see the file’s public URL; you can link to it from elsewhere.

---

## 6️⃣ Going Beyond (Optional Extras)

| Feature | How to Get It | Notes |
|---------|---------------|-------|
| **Image resizing / thumbnail** | Use Supabase’s image transformations (`?width=200&height=200`) in the image URL. | Great for profile thumbnails. |
| **Watermark** | Supabase doesn’t add watermarks, but you can use Cloudinary or Imgix before upload. | Requires a tiny script in Stacker or an external workflow. |
| **Delete Photo** | Add a “Delete” button that triggers a “DELETE” action on the image row. | Stacker handles this automatically if you use the built‑in UI. |
| **Private access** | Disable bucket public flag and use signed URLs. | Stacker can generate signed URLs automatically if you enable it in **Storage** settings. |

---

## 7️⃣ Troubleshooting Cheat‑Sheet

| Problem | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Images not saving | Improper bucket permissions | Check that the bucket is **public** or that you’re generating signed URLs. |
| Upload button disabled | Auth not set up | Make sure you’re logged in with the correct Auth provider. |
| No image preview | Wrong field type | Ensure the column is set to **Image** (not Text). |
| Incorrect path | Path template wrong | Double‑check `{{user.id}}` is used if you added a custom path. |

---

## That’s it! 🎉

You now have a fully functional profile photo upload feature powered by Supabase **without writing a single line of code**. If you’d rather use Directus, Webflow, or another no‑code tool, just let me know—I can map the same steps onto those platforms. Happy building!
